Title: Report by the Community Planning & Developm ent Department dated November 21 ,
Motion text: A. THAT first and second readings be given to Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 8204. B. THAT Bylaw No. 8204 be referred to a Public Hearing. The question on the motion was not called as [name removed] spoke to Delta’s Housing Action Plan and advised that reducing the number of parking spaces required for purpose - built rental buildings could help incentivize the development of rental stock, as it would help address the development community’s concern regarding the high c osts associated with constructing parking. [name removed] added that through the processing of devel opment applications, staff have learned that Delta’s parking ratios are generally higher than other cities. Therefore, staff have recommended to revise the current parking requirements by (i) reducing the parking rate for rental properties to 1.0 space per dwelling unit , (ii) reducing visitor parking spaces for all apartment buildings to 0.1 space per unit , and (iii) increasing the current permitted reduction of parking requirements along the Scott Road c orridor from 15 percent to 20 percent. T he Rapid Bus scheduled for 2023 will provide increased transit capacity to this area and therefore it may consequently decrease the need for private vehicles. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Community Planning & Develop ment Department dated November 23 ,
Motion text: A. THAT first, second and third readings be given to Development Application Procedures Bylaw No. 4918, 1992 Amendment Bylaw No. 8208. B. THAT first, second and third reading be given to Council Procedure Bylaw No. 5000, 2000 Amendment Bylaw No. 8205. C. THAT the amended Public Heari ng Protocol (Attachment C) be approved, subject to Council adoption of the above proposed bylaw amendments. D. THAT, should Council adopt the above proposed bylaw amendments, the updated typical process for zoning bylaws that are consistent with the Officia l Community Plan (Attachment D) be implemented for reports to Co uncil starting in January 2023. The question on the motion was not called as [name removed] spoke to recent changes to the Local Government Ac t as it relates to Public Hearings, to provide new housing more quickly, and to evaluate existing processes and policies in order to streamline applications. As a result of these l egislative changes, staff are recommending amendments to the Development Application Procedures Bylaw No. 4918, 1992, a nd the Council Procedure Bylaw No. 5000, 2000; the proposed amendments would permit rezoning applications that are consistent with the OCP to proceed without Public Hearing as determined by the Director of Com munity Planning and Development. These proposed amendments would not pre c lude Council from advancing an application through the Public Hearing process. In response to a Council query, M. Sangret advised that further details are forthcoming regarding how the Province is intending to e nact further leg islation that may look at the require ment of local governments to meet their housing needs in terms of delivery of units through application approvals. In response to a Council query regarding public engagement for development applications, M. Sangret spoke to Delta’s Development Application Procedure B ylaw No. 4918, 1992 which addresses different types of applications and their minimum requirements for notification, which include (i) a public notice sign on the property, (ii) n otification letters sent to residents within the immediate vicinity of the property, and (iii) for particular applications, a public information meeting may be held . [name removed] advised that d etails regarding applications can be found on Delta’s website , an d certain projects are placed on the “Let’s Talk Delta” virtual platform for public engagement . The question on motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Finance Department dated November 24, 2022 regarding 2023 to 2027 Financial Plan. (File: BL’s 8195 & 8196)
Motion text: A. THAT the 2023 Financial Plan be approved (Attachment A). B. THAT the Delta 2023 to 2027 Financial Plan Bylaw No. 8195, 2022 be given first, second and third readings (Attachment B). C. THAT the Development Cost Charge Reserve Funds Expenditure Bylaw No. 8196, 2022 be given first, second and third readings (Attachment C). The question on the motion was not called, as with the aid of a PowerPoint presentation, Melanie Kerr, Director of Finance, presented the 2023 Financial Plan, and remarked that the public consultation results revealed that 70% of the 700 comments received indicate good value for tax dollars. Regular Meeting– December 5, 2022 505 [name removed] then spoke to global economic pressures related to the ongoing pandemic recovery, increased inflation, and the need to invest in infrastructure. As a result of such factors, a 4.9% property tax increase is proposed, which includes a 3.4% increase for City services and a 1.5% increase for Community Infrastructure Investment; this represents a tax increase of approximately $197 for the average Delta homeowner. [name removed] advised that the overall proposed 2023 Financial Plan is $389.2 million, and contractual salary commitments and other non-discretionary inflationary increases can be attributed to the overall increase. In addressing Capital projects, M. Kerr advised that traffic calming and safety improvements, Parks, Recreation and Culture, and civic amenities are key investments. In response to a Council query, Sean McGill, City Manager, advised that surplus funding from the 2022 budget will be carried over and allocated to repair the Delta Senior Secondary School track and various other projects. As the newly elected Chair of the Metro Vancouver Board of Directors, Mayor Harvie advised that he has established a task force to address the anticipated substantial increase in utility costs. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Community Planning & Development Department dated November 17,
Topics: Neighbourhood character; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: A. THAT the following resolution regarding the proposal for a patio be provided to the Provincial Liquor and Cannabis Regulation Branch: “Be it resolved that: 1. In consideration of the location of the establishment, and the person capacity and hours of liquor service of the establishment, the Council of the City of Delta’s comments on regulatory criteria are as follows: a. The impact of noise on nearby residents. The Royal Canadian Legion, Branch No. 61 has operated a Temporary Expanded Service Area (TESA) patio since June 2020, with an aluminum- framed patio having been constructed for this space in April 2022. Over this period of time, staff have received no complaints. The proposed patio would occupy the same space as the TESA patio which is located immediately outside of the building on the public boulevard. Delta does not anticipate that the proposal would have any significant noise impacts on the surrounding business owners or patrons. b. The impact on the community if the application is approved. In addition to the points outlined in part “a.” above, the proposed patio does not encumber parking and has been designed to maintain a sidewalk for pedestrians beyond the patio area. Staff do not anticipate that the proposal will negatively impact the community. c. The view of residents and description of the method used to gather views. A letter informing the surrounding property owners and businesses within a 100 m radius was sent on October 5, 2022. To date, no correspondence has been received. 2. The Council of the City of Delta recommend the issuance of the structural change application for the following reasons: The request to establish a 28 m patio with an occupancy of 24 persons was found to support a rate of occupancy being consistent with other approved patio spaces in Delta (i.e., approximately 1.2 m of patio space per person). The proposal also aligns with the scope of the previously-approved TESA patio and does not reduce parking. Delta does not anticipate any significant increase in noise levels nor impacts on the community. Delta has consulted with the community within the immediate vicinity of the site and no comments were received.”

Motion text: THAT application LU009423 for an Official Community Plan amendment and rezoning at 5638 9A Avenue be denied. The question on the motion was not called as in response to queries from Council, Marcy Sangret, Deputy City Manager / Director of Community Planning and Development, advised that the application is for an Official Community Plan (OCP) amendment and rezoning to subdivide the subject property into two lots. [name removed] then commented on the rationale for denial, noting that the property is located in an existing mature neighbourhood that has not seen previous OCP amendments or rezoning applications, and the proposed density would be a significant change for the area. [name removed] then spoke to the feedback received from the community, which express opposition from 16 neighbouring households. In response to further queries from Council, M. Sangret advised that recent applications supported by Council in Tsawwassen did not include OCP amendments. Further, M. Sangret remarked that staff consider the neighbourhood, design, and community consultation when making application recommendations to Council. [name removed] stated that this application would be subject to a Public Hearing as an OCP amendment would be required to facilitate the proposal. [name removed] noted that should Council vote against the recommendation, staff would work with the applicant to refine the application. Discussion ensued, and Council discussed the merits of the application and staff rationale for denial. In response to a query from Council, M. Sangret clarified that the widths of the proposed lots would be 12.5 metres while other lot widths in the neighbourhood range from 15 to 30 metres. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Community Planning and Development Department dated January
Motion text: A. THAT the request for a Development Variance Permit to vary the maximum depth of a farm home plate measured from a dedicated road or street in Section 10.10.7(e)(i) of "Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600, 2017" be denied. B. THAT Development Variance Permit LU009429 be issued to vary the minimum side setback requirements in Section 10.10.4(b) of" Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600, 2017" for a new farm house subject to the following conditions: 1. THAT the new farm house be located on a farm home plate with a maximum depth of 60 m (197 ft) measured from a dedicated or constructed street; 2. THAT the applicant remove the deposited soil and fill and restore the subject area to its original condition; and 3. THAT the owners enter into a Section 219 Covenant for flood proofing and saving Delta harmless from all claims arising out of the proposed development and any events of flooding. C. THAT the application for a non-adhering residential use in the Agricultural Land Reserve at 3400 River Road West be refused. D. THAT the application for a soil or fill use in the Agricultural Land Reserve at 3400 River Road West be refused. E. THAT the Mayor and City Clerk be authorized to sign all documents pertaining to this development. The question on the motion was not called as in response to queries from Council, M. Sangret advised that the proposal includes three separate applications for the construction of a new farm house, which consists of (i) a development variance permit to vary the side setback and farm home plate depth requirements, (ii) an Agricultural Land Commission application for non-adhering residential use within the Agricultural Land Reserve, and (iii) an Agricultural Land Commission application for soil or fill use within the Agricultural Land Reserve. [name removed] clarified that a Stop Work Order was issued as a result of unauthorized soil deposit on site. [name removed] referred to the On Table correspondence that clarified that only a partial amount of soil had been deposited. [name removed] further advised that the variance requested is not minor in nature, as its purpose is to relocate the farm home plate in order to have a depth of 150 metres; the standard depth of a farm home plate is 60 metres. [name removed] noted that the current regulations were adopted following consultation with Delta’s agricultural community on farmhouse size requirements and farm home plates in an effort to mitigate the construction of large homes on agricultural land. The Agricultural Land Commission regulates the size of farmhouse dwellings and additional dwellings, but does not regulate farm home plates. [name removed] remarked that there have been few instances where Minutes – Regular Meeting – February 6, 2023 41 Council has considered relocation of a farm home plate. As such, M. Sangret advised that it is recommended that the application for soil or fill use be denied as it is relative to the construction of a proposed new farmhouse. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Corporate Services Department dated February 21, 2023 regarding Delta’s Social Action Plan 2023 - 2028 .
Motion text: A. THAT the Delta Social Action Plan 2023 - 2028 be endorsed, substantially in the form of Attachment [name removed] – Regular Meeting – March 6, 2023 77 B. THAT, consistent with research findings and feedback from community groups and Delta residents, work related to the following issues be prioritized for 2023 - 24: i. Thriving children and youth - explore opportunities for providing increased integrated services for youth and their families - mental health, substance use, education, training, housing, employment and other community and social services - potentially thro ugh collaboration with community partners on a neighbourhood or youth hub in Delta. ii. Active and engaged seniors - complete an age - friendly assessment of the Delta community and develop an action plan to support seniors to age in place and live active lives. iii. Safe and resilient Delta - enhance community capacity to address racism and discrimination, strengthen community resilience and emergency preparedness, and increase safe mobility options for residents. iv. Inclusive Delta - work with community partners to enhance settlement services for immigrants and refugees in Delta. C. THAT staff report back annually on the progress made in implementing the actions of the Social Action Plan. The question on the motion was not called as Mel Cheesman, General Manager, Corporate Services, introduc ed the Social Action Plan 2023 – 2028 and highlighted the extensive public consultation process , which resulted in finalizing the seven strategic direction s . [name removed] also advised that over 42% of the 190 action items identified in the Plan have been completed. Olga Shcherbyna, Corporate Social Planner, with the aid of a PowerPoint presentation , provided an update on social planning in Delta, including the Delta Social Action Pla n, and its implementation and priorities. [name removed] advised that the two - year public engagement process concluded in 2022, and an overarching theme emerged: Delta residents love the community character, diversity , and C ity services offered , while publi c transit, youth - friendly places, housing affordability, and community connections were identified as current challenges. [name removed] further advised that the title of the plan , “Mobilizing and Driving Equity in Delta , ” indicates empathy for the most vul nerable, and includes the following seven priorities: (i) City of Delta – l eading the c hange, (ii) healthy Delta, (iii) thriving children and youth, (iv) safe and resilient Delta, (v) active and engaged seniors, (vi) housing and caring for Delta, and (vii) inclusive and accessible Delta. [name removed] concluded that staff continue to monitor grant opportunities for potential funding to compliment the $670,000 already raised for community services. Minutes – Regular Meeting – March 6, 2023 78 In response to a Council query, O. Shcherbyna advised that the Delta School District provides services through the Delta Settlement Workers Progr am, and has increased the number of multicultural workers within Delta schools in order to better support refugees . [name removed] added that staff and community partners continue to explore options to bridge the gap in services in relation to families, and residents who are not enrolled at a Delta school . Staff will liaise with the Guru Nanak Food Bank to inquire what additional se rvices are needed by newcomers. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Development Department dated April 13, 2023 regarding Six - Storey Mixed - Use Building Proposal at 11996 70 Avenue (1176122 B.C. LTD).
Motion text: A. THAT first, second and third readings be given to Zoning Amendment Bylaw No. 8226. B. THAT the application for Development Variance Permit LU009094 be received . C. THAT the application for Developm ent Permit LU009094 be received. D. THAT the owner satisfy the following requirements as a condition of final consideration and adoption, and permit issuance: 1. Enter into legal agreements to the satisfaction of the Director of Development for the following: a. a. Building and landscape design; b. Provision of cash - in - lieu of park land in the amount of five percent of the value of the land prior to registration of a Stata Subdivision Plan; c. Update the existing 4.6 m wide utility statutory right - of - way J24794 to include provision for public pedestrian access over the statutory right - of - way area; and d. Prohibition of roof top telecommunications equipment without permission from the City of Delta. 2. Enter into legal agreements to the satisfaction of the General Manager of Engineering for the following: a. Development Agreement for site servicing including: i. A condition that the development must connect to the new sanitary pump station to be constructed by Delta; ii. Requirements for stormwater management consistent with the Cougar Creek Integrated Stormwater Management Plan incorporating best management practices for on - site infiltration for rainwater and stormwater runoff reduction, and the provision of any capacity upgrades required to the municipal stor m water management system to service the proposed development; b. Statutory right - of - way with a 1.5 m width to accommodate future road frontage improvements along 120 Street; c. Geotechnical covenant with technical recommendations prepared by a qualified professional related to the proposed construction, and conditions to save Delta harmless from all claims arising from the proposed development; and Minutes – Regular Meeting – May 1 , 2023 139 d. Highway Use Permit for any proposed temporary soil anchors within municipal road dedication or statutory rights - of - way, including provision of security related to the removal of the soil anchors. 3. Provide road dedication to meet or exceed the requirements of the "Delta Subdivision and Development Standards Bylaw No. 7162, 2015" including: a. An additional approximately 2 m for a total 17 m of road dedication as measured from the legal centreline of 120 Street with a corner cut of 6 m by 6 m at the intersection of 120 Street and 70 Avenue; and b. A corner cut of 3 m by 3 mat the intersection of 70 Avenue and the lane to the west of the site. 4. Provide a final landscape plan and a comprehensive sign plan to the satisfaction of the Director of Development. 5. Provide cash - in - lieu in the amount of $50,000 for signalization improvement at the intersection of Nicholson Road and 70 Avenue, and $99,050 for the development's portion of the sanitary flows being directed to the new municipal sanitary sewer pump station. 6. Provide payment of the following securities in amounts acceptable to the Director of Development: a. For landscaping and tree planting; and b. Other securities including a geotechnical security as required by Staff or Council. 7 Provide a Park, Recreation and Culture Amenity Contribution in the amount of $1,000 per unit for a total of $90,000. The question on the motion was not called as i n response to a query from Council, Doreann Mayhew, Acting Director of Development, advised that prior to final adoption, the Applicant would be required to provide a stormwater manage ment plan . In response to further queries from Council, Marcy Sangret, Deputy City Manager, advised that the height of the proposed building is compliant with Delta’s Official Community Plan and a Public Hearing is not required. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Community Planning Department dated May 8, 2023 regarding Neighbourhood Petition Rezoning – 110 Street between 78 and 79A Avenue .
Motion text: THAT the rezoning application process described in this report be applied to the petition from residents of 110 Street, between 78 Avenue and 79A Avenue. The question on the motion was not called as Marcy Sangret, Deputy City Manager, provided background information on the Neighbourhood Petition and Rezoning Procedure, noting that it was initiated after a group of residents submitted a petition in 2004 to rezone their properties, in an effort to prevent single detached dwellings larger than 232 m ; the procedure required a minimum threshold of 75 percent support by landowners in the subject area. [name removed] advised that the current request is from property owners located on either side of 110 Street, between 78 Avenue and 79A Avenue, who are seeking Council’s approval to rez one their properties to RS4, which would remove restrictions related to house size, setbacks, and secondary suite requirements; a formal application would be required and an application fee would be applied. Minutes – Regular Meeting – May 29 , 2023 164 Additio nally , M . Sangret remarked that neighbouring properties would be notified through direct mail . Title: Bus Rapid Transit Action Plan
Motion text: A. WHEREAS TransLink and the Mayors’ Council on Regional Transportation unanimously endorsed the Access for Everyone Plan (also called Transport 2050: 10-Year Priorities ) in 2022 to urgently expand and improve transit throughout Metro Vancouver to support record-setting population growth, housing affordability, GHG emission reduction targets and reconciliation; B. WHEREAS the Access for Everyone Plan places a strong emphasis on quick and cost-effective, delivery of new at-grade rapid transit through nine new Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridors throughout the region; C. WHEREAS the Access for Everyone Plan identified a new BRT line along the Scott Road Corridor to enhance livability and transportation in the City of Delta and City of Surrey; D. WHEREAS BRT requires the allocation of road space and reconfiguring of roads for successful implementation; E. WHEREAS Municipalities are the primary administrators of local and regional roads in the region and will be crucial partners in the successful implementation of future BRT corridors; F. WHEREAS TransLink and the Mayors’ Council are currently undertaking a prioritization exercise to determine the order in which BRT corridors will be implemented that emphasizes a ‘work with the willing’ approach so that first phase of BRT projects can be built quickly and to a high quality, with maximum support from municipal and other local government partners, to serve as a showcase for this type of rapid transit to the rest of the region; Be it resolved, THAT the City of Delta supports a BRT line featuring dedicated bus lanes, transit signal priority, enhanced customer amenities at stations and specialized vehicles to support fast, reliable, high-quality rapid transit to along the Scott Road Corridor; THAT City of Delta support for this project will include: 1. Working with TransLink to finalize and sign a Bus Rapid Transit Action Plan Commitment Framework to partner with TransLink to expeditiously achieve a high quality BRT corridor; 2. A commitment to deliver a BRT with near continuous exclusive transit lane along the length of the corridor, achieved primarily through reallocation of existing road space; 3. Support for prioritizing transit, including willingness to reallocate space from parking, changes to property access, turn restrictions, and transit signal priority; 4. Willingness to allocate, resources, and in-kind support; 5. Appointing a BRT “Council champion,” a BRT internal staff lead, and dedicated staff team to support the project through all phases; Minutes – Regular Meeting – September 11, 2023 293 6. Willingness to expedite processes, permits and approvals, and to co-lead and support public engagement; 7. Aligning local plans and policies to support Transit Oriented Communities and implement supportive infrastructure including walking and cycling networks. THAT Delta Council direct staff to work expediently with TransLink and coordinate with adjacent municipalities towards the planning, design and implementation of BRT within the municipality; THAT Delta Council ask the Mayors’ Council to prioritize the Scott Road Corridor as a priority BRT project, based on the municipality’s readiness to support the project.

Title: Report by the Community Planning Department dated October 3, 2023 regarding Provincial Housing Target and Action Plan . (File: P23-19)
Motion text: A. THAT the action plan to achieve Delta's provincially-mandated housing target be endorsed. B. THAT regular updates be provided to Council on progress toward achieving the housing target, coinciding with the reporting milestones established in the Provincial Order. The question on the motion was not called as [name removed] provided an overview of the provincial housing target, noting that the housing target set for Delta is 3,607 net new units in the next five years; this target represents 75 percent of projected housing needs in Delta. [name removed] then spoke to proposed actions the City can take to achieve the housing target, and the anticipated rate of growth. It was noted that progress reports are required and the Province may implement other tools should they determine that the City may not meet the target. [name removed] then offered background information on the Housing Accelerator Fund, noting that the City has submitted an application. Discussion took place and Council commented on (i) public input opportunities, including the receipt of written submissions in instances where Public Hearings are not required, (ii) opportunities for future community amenities as a result of development, and (iii) future growth throughout all of Delta’s unique communities. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Corporate Services Department dated December 4, 2023 regarding
Motion text: A. THAT Delta Development cost charges Bylaw No. 7560, 2017 Amendment Bylaw No. 8292, 202-3 be amended as outlined in this report to update the development cost charge rates to reflect feedback received during the stakeholder and public consultation process; B. THAT Delta Development cost charges Bylaw No. 7560, 2017, Amendment Bylaw No. 8292, 2023 be given second reading, as amended; Minutes – Regular Meeting – December 11, 2023 452 C. THAT Delta Development cost charges Bylaw No. 7560, 2017 Amendment Bylaw No. 8292, 2023 be given third reading; and D. THAT Delta Development cost charges Bylaw No. 7560, 2017 Amendment Bylaw No. 8292, 2023 be forwarded to the Province of British Columbia for Statutory Approval by the Inspector of Municipalities. The question on the motion was not called as in response to queries from Council, M. Sangret spoke to low density residential development cost charges. In particular, it was noted that the development cost charge for a single detached dwelling is $11,942 for each new lot; the proposed new development cost charges (DCC) for such construction would be $14,225 in the first year the Bylaw takes effect and subsequently $19,342 thereafter. This represents an increase of approximately 62% for single family dwellings over two years. Given that the City’s development cost charges have not seen a major update for a number of years, staff propose that rates across all categories increase at varying proportions. For low density residential, which include single family dwellings, a 20% municipal assist factor is proposed in the first year that will be reduced to 1% in subsequent years. [name removed] advised that the City is mandated to provide a municipal assist factor and has offered 10% in the past; a one-time 20% municipal assist factor is proposed given that low density residential DCC will increase 62%. Discussion ensued regarding the definition of “Intensive Agriculture” and concerns shared by the Delta Farmers’ Institute (DFI). [name removed] remarked that certain types of agriculture operations are most robust, and therefore utilize municipal infrastructure on a larger scale. [name removed] further noted that not all agriculture uses are subject to DCC; for instance, farm dwellings and certain types of barns are not subject to DCC, and other uses are subject to a lower DCC rate as their operations are not industrial scaled. With regard to DFI’s concerns, M. Sangret advised that staff examined excluding the growing area in the Intensive Agriculture DCC rate; however it was not recommended as it would not reflect the impact of the operations on the City’s infrastructure. [name removed] then spoke to the proposed Intensive Agriculture rates, noting that staff believe the revised rate captures a balance between the impacts of the operations on the City’s infrastructure and the concerns raised by DFI. [name removed] also highlighted that the proposed rates will be phased-in and existing applications will be grandfathered at former rates. In response to queries from the Chair, D. van Dyk spoke to next steps, noting the Bylaw is subject to approval by the Inspector of Municipalities; should Council wish that staff continue to examine the proposed DCC rates, a Council resolution would be valuable. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: Report by the Parks, Recreation and Culture and Communication and Engagement Departments dated February 27, 2024 regarding Winskill Aquatic and Fitness
Motion text: A. THAT the existing Winskill Aquatic and Fitness Centre be replaced with a new purpose- built aquatics and fitness centre. B. THAT staff be directed to issue requests for proposals for an architect and construction manager to proceed with the replacement of the facility. C. THAT staff be directed to commence a community engagement program to obtain input from user groups, Delta residents and neighbours. Jim Bauer, Director, Capital Projects, provided background information on the Winskill Aquatic and Fitness Centre, noting that it is the oldest indoor facility in Delta. [name removed] advised that studies have been conducted over the past four years with regard to funding, as well as the notion to replace or to renovate the facility. [name removed] then commented on the analysis that was conducted on the current structure and confirmed that it would cost approximately $130 million to renovate or replace it. [name removed] also highlighted that, should Council opt to replace the facility, it would allow for the current facility to remain open during construction and greater options for meeting the long-term needs of the community. [name removed] then spoke to the financial considerations and advised that the project would be funded through borrowing through the Recreational Capital Investment Levy, as well as development cost charges. JoAnne Kleb, Manager of Engagement, spoke to the proposed community engagement effects, noting that it would be conducted in three phases – (i) raise awareness of the need for a new facility, (ii) engage on features, and (iii) engage to finalize aesthetics. [name removed] highlighted that staff would bring awareness to residents through the use of Let’s Talk Delta and local newspapers. [name removed] provided an overview of the anticipated timeline of the project, advising that staff would report to Council following the conclusion of each engagement phase, which would take place in 2024, and that the new facility be anticipated to open in the summer of 2027. Minutes – Regular Council – March 11, 2024 Mayor Harvie emphasized the importance of presenting a draft architectural design to Council for comment and approval prior to the commencement of the construction phase. In response to queries from Council, J. Kleb advised that public engagement would be in-person to allow residents an opportunity to meet with staff and share their ideas. Mayor Harvie emphasized his support for a new facility, however, expressed concern with regard to (i) the proposal for eight pool lanes instead of ten , (ii) the location of the proposal facility, highlighting that he does not want to use field space to accommodate the construction , and (iii) the lack of parking at the current facility, citing a possible expansion area on the south side of the lot. The question on the motion was then called.

Title: A. THAT Council receive the consultation process summary as outlined in this report a…
Motion text: A. THAT Council receive the consultation process summary as outlined in this report and consider the feedback received during the public consultation process included in Attachments B and C. B. THAT first and second readings be given to City of Delta Official Community Plan 2024: Housing Our Future Bylaw No. 8400. C. THAT Bylaw No. 8400 be confirmed as being consistent with the Current Financial Plan and the Liquid and Solid Waste Management Plans, as required by the Local Government Act . D. THAT Bylaw No. 8400 be referred to the Agricultural Land Commission for comment to confirm compliance with the Agricultural Land Commission Act. E. THAT Bylaw No. 8400 be referred to a Public Hearing to be scheduled on April 22, 2024 at 3:00 pm at Delta City Hall, 4500 Clarence Taylor Crescent. W ith the aid of a PowerPoint presentation, JoAnne Kleb, Manager, Engagement, provided an overview of the engagement process for the Official Community Plan (OCP) , and Doreann Mayhew, General Manager, Development, provided additional information on the engagement process highlighting that the City’s Housing Action Plan was integrated into the draft OCP . [name removed] then reviewed comments and feedback received with re gard to (i) infrastructure, (ii) traffic and transportation, (iii) public services and amenities, (iv) environment and natural spaces, (v) community character, (vi) community involvement, (vii) specific properties, and (viii) lobby senior governments. [name removed] concluded by highlighting that the OCP does not change the underl y ing zoning, and that there will continue to be opportunities for the public to engage on projects . In response to queries from Council, D. Mayhew advised that (i) should the application receive first and second reading, a Public Hearing notice would be mailed all Delta residents, (ii) the draft OCP consolidates the current land use designations from 80 to 10, ( iii ) there are no proposed changes to industrial and agriculture la nd uses, and ( i v) the Province is requiring cities to update their OCPs every five years. In response to queries from Council regarding infrastructure, Steven Lan, General Manager, Engineering, advised that staff are updating models for key corridors ; and there has been extensive work conducted over the last decade to provide services for a growing community . The question on the motion was then called.

Title: British Columbia’s Decriminalization Policy Updates - Updated Exemption to Address Public Drug Use
Motion text: THAT the presentation regarding British Columbia’s Decriminalization Policy Updates - Updated Exemption to Address Public Drug Use be received for information. Police Chief Neil Dubord, Delta Police Department (DPD) , a dvised that in January 2023 , changes were made to the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act (the “Act”) that decriminalize the possession of various drugs under 2.5 grams. Chief Dubord further advised that the DPD has monitored the exemption and was of the opinion that a program must be implemented that provides additional services to the community with regard to drug addiction, in order for decriminalization to be effective. Chief Dubord then advised that additional changes were made to the Act in May 2024 that prohibit s the use of drugs in public spaces and require s users to use in private residence’ or healthcare facilit ies , otherwise known as safe injection sites. Chief Dubord noted that the Province will be providing training to officers that will assist with effectively managing the new protocol. Chief Dubord will report back to Council in the fall with an update regarding lack of safe injection sites .

Title: Expanded Public Engagement for the 2025 Budget Process
Motion text: Whereas, public engagement is essential for ensuring transparency, accountability, and inclusivity in the municipal decision - making process; and Whereas, the City of Delta is committed to fostering a culture of openness and collaboration between residents and local government; and Whereas, the upcoming 2025 budget process presents an opportunity to enhance public participation and understanding of municipal finances; Therefore, be it resolved that: 1. Council will hold public budget workshops, allowing residents to observe discussions and deliberations on bu dgetary matters. 3. The City of Delta will expand opportunities to solicit feedback from residents on budget priorities and spending allocations. 4. Title: A. THAT the following resolution be submitted to the Federation of Canadian Municipal…
Motion text: A. THAT the following resolution be submitted to the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) for consideration at its 2025 Annual Conference. WHEREAS local governments across Canada have the authority to regulate the sale and use of fireworks within their respective jurisdictions ; WHEREAS significant discrepancies exist among municipal, provincial, and federal regulations governing the sale and use of fireworks, compounded by the availability of fireworks through online purchases from sources outside provincial and national borders ; AND WHEREAS the irresponsible acquisition and use of fireworks contribute to personal injuries, property damage, environmental harm, and risks to pets, livestock and wildlife . THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Federation of Canadian Municipalities urge the federal government to work collaboratively with provinces, territories, and local governments to establish a comprehensive framework to address the online sale and importation of fireworks into Canada, su pporting consistent regulations and improving public safety. B. THAT the Federation of Canadian Municipalities resolution set out in Recommendation A be shared with Delta's MP, MLAs, the BC Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General and BC Minister of Agriculture and Food.

Title: Suitability of Shoreline Area for Scattering and Immersing Ashes
Motion text: WHEREAS there has been a long - standing request from the Indian Diaspora living in Delta for space on the Fraser River shoreline to be able to immerse the ashes of their departed loved ones in the flowing water ; WHEREAS for many, scattering ashes in a meaningful location can be an important part of the grieving process and can reflect the deceased’s life, values or preferences ; AND WHEREAS the Five River Management Services Society has identified the public trail network with access to the Fraser River, located in the Delta Link Business Park as a most suitable site. THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED THAT: 1. Delta staff report back to Council on the suitability of the City of Delta’s existing shoreline area of the public trail connecting the Delta Link Business Park to the Fraser River as a City of Delta site for the purpose of having families scattering or immersing ashes of their loved ones. 2. The report from staff include costs to make suitable improvements to the shoreline area to accommodate the proposed shared use of the proposed location. 3. The City Manager consult with the Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs for possible grant opportunities.

Title: Development Cost Charges
Topics: Development; Taxes & spending; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: WHEREAS the residen tial and commercial development ac tivity has significantly stalled as a result of increases in prices for building materials, skilled labour, higher financing costs and scheduled 2025 increases to City of Delta, Metro Vancouver and Translink development cost charges; WHEREAS City of Delta’s development cost charges are collected from the development community at either time of subdivision applica tion or issuance of a building permit depending on the land use category; Minutes – Regular Council – January 20, 2025 AND WHEREAS the Honourable Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs has advised that Provincial Legisla tion needs to be amended to allow Local Governments to consider changing the time for colle ctio n of development cost charges . THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT : 1. The City Manager be directed to have appropriate staff conduct a financial analysis on delaying collec tion of all development cost charges to time of issuance of occupancy permit instead of at time of subdivision applica tion or issuance of a building permit depending on the land use category. 2. Council request the Honourable Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs to consider amendments to applicable legisla tion in order to allow Local Governments to consider changing the time for collec tion of development cost charges. 3. Council request the Metro Vancouver Board of Directors, TransLink Mayors Council and Board of Directors also consider changing the time for collec tion of development cost charges.

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT : 1. Title: Internal Audit Function (Submission from Mayor George V. Harvie)
Motion text: WHEREAS the City of Delta 2 025 Financial Plan includes Total Expenditures of $552,267,000; AND WHEREAS many local governments have recognized the need to have an internal audit function to ensure the protection of public tax dollars; AND WHEREAS an internal audit function in the Cit y of Delta would ensure public funds are used appropriately, accurately tracked, and aligned with budgetary allocation; AND WHEREAS with half a billion dollar of annual expenditures in the City of Delta it is essential that the City’s Finance Department ha s the resources of an internal audit function for maintaining transparency, accountability, and efficiency in public finances. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: The City Manager and General Manager Finance include in the 2026 Draft Financial Plan the provisio n of an internal audit function in the Finance Department for Council’s consideration.

Title: Tree Protection in Sunshine Hills submitted by Councillor Kruger
Topics: Environment & climate; Neighbourhood character; Public services
Motion text: WHEREAS the Sunshine Hills neighbourhood is defined by its mature tree canopy, which is central to the character, livability, and environmental health of the community; WHEREAS increasing redevelopment pressures stemming from provincial legis lative changes are resulting in the removal of large, mature trees, leading to concerns from residents that the unique character of Sunshine Hills is being eroded; WHEREAS while Delta has a citywide Tree Protection and Replacement Bylaw, residents of Sunsh ine Hills have expressed a desire for stronger, neighbourhood - specific protections to preserve their unique tree canopy; WHEREAS under the current framework of the Community Charter, municipalities cannot use tree bylaws to override the development potenti al of a property permitted under zoning regulations; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. Staff be directed to consult with the Sunshine Hills community to develop a Neighbourhood Tree Protection Pilot Program, which may include: o Establishing a Heritage Tree designation to protect landmark trees of significant size, age, or community value. o Enhanced tree replacement requirements or higher cash - in - lieu contributions within Sunshine Hills to better reflect the value of lost mature trees. o A clear opt - in mechanism for neighbourhoods like Sunshine Hills that wish to adopt stronger protections while ensuring consistency within the community. o Education and incentive programs for homeowners to preserve large trees during redevelopment. o Enhanced reporting on the number of heritage trees impacted by development and replacement trees required. 2. Staff report back to council on the results of this community engagement by February 28, 2026. 3. The City of Delta write to the Minister of Municipal Affairs requesting amendments to t he Community Charter to provide municipalities with greater authority to protect mature trees in established neighbourhoods, even in areas where redevelopment is permitted.

Title: Examination of the City of Delta as part of the core city services urgent and primary care centres servicing North and South Delta
Motion text: Whereas access to timely and appropriate primary and urgent care is essential for the health and well - being of all residents of Delta; and Whereas many residents of North and South De lta face challenges accessing primary care physicians and experience long wait times at Delta Hospital Emergency Department for non - emergency medical needs; and Whereas, establishing UPCC’s as core City Services in North and South Delta would greatly impro ve access to care, reduce current strain on the Delta Hospital Emergency Department and enhance the overall health of our community; and Whereas a comprehensive analysis is required to determine the feasibility, costs, and potential benefits of such a serv ice. THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT 1. Staff be directed to initiate a procurement process for the selection of a qualified consultant to conduct a detailed analysis of the feasibility of the City of Delta establishing UPCC’s as part of its core services, ope rating in both North and South Delta. 2. The analysis should include, but not be limited to: o An assessment of the current gaps in primary and urgent care access in North and South Delta. o A review of successful UPCC’s models in other cities. o A detailed cost an alysis, including capital and operating costs, and potential funding sources. o Recommendations on an optimal model for UPCC’s in Delta, including service delivery, staffing, use of appropriate City Departments for operational support and governance

Title: Addressing Downloading of Provincial and Federal Responsibilities submitted by Counc illor Kruger
Motion text: WHEREAS senior levels of government have not adequately supported, provided or funded essential services under their jurisdiction, including accessible health care, hospitals, social services, p olice services, non - market housing, and critical infrastructure projects such as dike upgrades, secondary channel dredging, and a River Road overpass; AND WHEREAS municipalities increasingly face the burden of funding provincial or federal areas of respons ibility in order to address service gaps, a practice commonly referred to as downloading, wherein senior governments shift their obligations, whether financial or otherwise, onto local governments; AND WHEREAS the City of Vancouver reported in 2021 and 202 2 that downloading from senior governments results in an estimated $250 million per year in additional operating and capital costs; AND WHEREAS the financial burden transferred to the City of Delta ultimately impacts municipal taxpayers, creating pressure for increased property taxes and fees; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT staff provide a report on the financial impacts of downloading including the cumulative costs associated with provincial and federal responsibilities that have shifted to the City of Delta over time; BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the rep ort includes, but is not limited to, costs related to health and social services, housing, homelessness response, mental health and addiction supports, police services, critical infrastructure upgrades, and any other areas where the City is funding or is c onsidering funding responsibilities traditionally held by senior levels of government.

Title: Fraser River Tunnel Project Agriculture Enhancement Fund
Motion text: WHEREAS the Fraser River Tunnel Project is a critical provincial infrastructure initiative to address congestion along Highway 99, enhance regional mobility and public safety, and support the efficient movement of goods, services, and people, and Delta Council recognizes that the replacement of the George Massey Tunnel and similar projects are necessary to sustain economic growth and benefit the local, regional, and provincial e conomy; AND WHEREAS the Environmental Assessment for the project notes it is expected to impact approximately 21.5 hectares of agricultural land in one of British Columbia’s most productive farming regions, including about 3.2 hectares permanently removed from agricultural use and 18.3 hectares temporarily affected during construction, with potential implications for regional food security and the provincial agricultural economy; AND WHEREAS mitigation measures have been proposed to reduce impacts to agricu ltural land, and Delta has provided comments to the Agricultural Land Commission emphasizing the need to protect soil quality, address cumulative and long - term effects, and ensure that any restoration plan maintains the long - term agricultural productivity of affected lands. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Mayor, on behalf of Council, write to the Minister of Agriculture and Food and the Minister of Transportation and Transit requesting that the Province consider establishing a Fraser River Tunnel Project specific Agricultural Enhancement Fund to offset temporary and permanent impacts, including those impacts during preliminary works, to agricultural land and productivity and to support long - term reinvestment in local agricultural infrastructure, soil enhan cement, drainage improvements, and overall farm viability initiatives.

Title: Motion regarding Funding for Agricultural Land Commission (ALC)
Motion text: WHEREAS the Agricu ltural Land Commission (ALC) is a cornerstone of protecting British Columbia’s finite and irreplaceable agricultural land base, yet has been compelled to reduce staffing levels solely as a result of inadequate and insufficient provincial funding; AND WHE REAS these staffing reductions significantly impair the ALC’s ability to fulfill its legislated mandate, weaken regulatory oversight, and reflect a serious failure by the Province to prioritize agricultural protection amid escalating pressures on food secu rity, farmland loss, and the long - term viability of the agriculture sector; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Union of BC Municipalities formally convey its strong concern to the Government of British Columbia that chronic provincial underfunding has dir ectly resulted in staffing cuts at the ALC and has undermined confidence in the Province’s commitment to safeguarding agricultural land; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the Province of British Columbia be urgently called upon to immediately restore, stab ilize, and significantly increase funding to the Agricultural Land Commission, and to unequivocally recognize and act upon the protection of agricultural land and the agriculture sector as a critical and non - negotiable provincial priority.

Title: Independent Revie w of the Fraser River Tunnel Project
Topics: Taxes & spending; Transportation; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: WHEREAS the Province of British Columbia has announced that it has terminated negotiations with Cross Fraser Partnership for the final construction phase of the Fraser River Tunnel Project and will restart procurement through a new contracting model; AND WHEREAS the Province has confirmed that agreement could not be reached on the commercial terms required to proceed with final construction; AND WHEREAS the Fraser River Tunnel Project is one of the most significant transportation infrastructure projects in British Columbia and is critical to the movement of people, goods and services throughout Delta, Metro Vancouver and the province; AND WHEREAS residents, businesses, municipalities and taxpayers deserve transparency regarding the financial, scheduling and procurement implications of this decision; AND WHEREAS the Province has not publicly disclosed the revised project budget, the anticipated increase in project costs, or a revised project completion date resulting from the termination of the procurement process; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Delta Council formally request the Province of British Columbia appoint an independent third party to review the circumstances tha t led to the termination of the procurement process for the Fraser River Tunnel Project; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the review include: 1. The reasons negotiations with Cross Fraser Partnership were unsuccessful; 2. The financial implications of terminating the existing procurement process; 3. The total costs incurred to date on project planning, design, procurement and early works; 4. The anticipated revised project budget; 5. The anticipated revised project completion date; 6. The impacts of the procurement restart on regional transportation, goods movement and economic development; 7. Recommendations to improve transparency and accountability for future major transportation infrastructure procurements; 8. Rationale as to why federal infrastructure grant funding was decline d by the Province; and 9. Consideration of revis iting the design to a bridge. AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Delta Council request the Province publicly release the findings of the review and provide regular updates on the revised project budget, schedule an d procurement process; AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT Metro Vancouver member jurisdictions be requested to support Delta Council’s advocacy efforts regarding the Fraser River Tunnel Project, including calls for greater transparency, accountability, and en gagement from the Province on project funding, procurement, timing, transportation impacts, and regional growth implications.
